parts.name: body loop

physics.Basic_description: The main D-shaped loop of the carabiner, featuring a matte black anodized aluminum finish and a curved spine.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing capacity for attaching to ropes or gear.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper would firmly grasp the spine or the straight side of the loop to stabilize the object.
physics.reason: Carabiner bodies are typically forged or machined from solid metal stock to ensure structural integrity under load.

parts.description: The main D-shaped loop of the carabiner, featuring a matte black anodized aluminum finish and a curved spine.
parts.function: Provides the primary structural strength and load-bearing capacity for attaching to ropes or gear.

parts.name: nose lug

physics.Basic_description: A small protrusion at the nose of the carabiner body, matching the black anodized finish of the main loop.
physics.Functional_description: Engages with the gate latch to secure the gate in the closed position.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integrated into the body to be a primary grasp point; would be avoided during manipulation.
physics.reason: Integral part of the solid forged body structure.

parts.description: A small protrusion at the nose of the carabiner body, matching the black anodized finish of the main loop.
parts.function: Engages with the gate latch to secure the gate in the closed position.

parts.name: gate bar

physics.Basic_description: The straight swinging bar that closes the opening, finished in matte black anodized aluminum.
physics.Functional_description: Swings open to allow attachment of gear and closes to secure the connection.
physics.Grasped_description: Can be grasped to manually open the gate, though care must be taken not to pinch fingers against the body.
physics.reason: Gate bars are solid metal rods or extrusions to withstand lateral loading.

parts.description: The straight swinging bar that closes the opening, finished in matte black anodized aluminum.
parts.function: Swings open to allow attachment of gear and closes to secure the connection.

parts.name: gate latch

physics.Basic_description: A small cylindrical component at the tip of the gate, appearing as part of the gate assembly in black.
physics.Functional_description: Interfaces with the nose lug to lock or guide the gate closure.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small to grasp independently; manipulation would occur via the gate bar.
physics.reason: Small machined metal component, solid by necessity of size and function.

parts.description: A small cylindrical component at the tip of the gate, appearing as part of the gate assembly in black.
parts.function: Interfaces with the nose lug to lock or guide the gate closure.

parts.name: hinge pin

physics.Basic_description: A small pin visible at the hinge point, likely steel, appearing dark grey or black.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the pivot axis allowing the gate to swing open and closed.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a graspable feature; it is a small mechanical fastener embedded in the hinge.
physics.reason: Pins are solid metal cylinders to provide shear strength.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
